overview: Ukraine is the largest country lying entirely within Europe. Its capital and largest city is Kyiv. Ukraine became independent when the Soviet Union broke up in 1991. Since 2014 parts of the country, including Crimea, have been occupied by Russia, and in 2022 Russia launched a full-scale invasion. Ukrainian is the official language.

geography.text: Most of Ukraine is flat, fertile plain with rich black soil, which has made it one of the world's great grain-growing countries. The Dnieper river flows through the middle of the country, past Kyiv, to the Black Sea. The Carpathian Mountains rise in the far west and the Crimean Mountains in the south. Ukraine has coastlines on the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov.

history.text: Kyiv was the centre of Kievan Rus', a powerful medieval state, until it was destroyed by the Mongols in 1240. Ukrainian lands were later divided between Poland–Lithuania, the Cossacks and Russia. Under Soviet rule, millions died in the famine of 1932–33, known as the Holodomor. Ukraine became independent in 1991; Russia annexed Crimea in 2014 and launched a full-scale invasion in 2022.

events.title: Christianity adopted
events.text: Volodymyr the Great makes Kievan Rus' Christian.

events.title: Cossack uprising
events.text: Bohdan Khmelnytsky leads a revolt against Polish rule.

events.title: The Holodomor
events.text: A man-made famine under Soviet rule kills millions of Ukrainians.

government.text: Ukraine is a semi-presidential republic. The President, elected directly, is head of state and commander-in-chief. The Verkhovna Rada, the parliament, chooses the Prime Minister. Since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022, Ukraine has been under martial law, and elections have been postponed. It became a candidate to join the European Union in 2022.

economy.text: Ukraine has some of the most fertile soil in the world and is a major exporter of grain, sunflower oil and corn, earning it the nickname 'the breadbasket of Europe'. It also has steel and IT industries. The war has caused enormous damage to its cities, ports and power plants.

culture.text: Ukrainian culture is famous for embroidered shirts called vyshyvanka, painted Easter eggs called pysanky and borscht, a beetroot soup listed by UNESCO in 2022. Kyiv's St Sophia Cathedral dates from the 1000s. Taras Shevchenko is the national poet.

items.title: Pysanky
items.text: Easter eggs decorated with wax and dye.

items.title: Borscht
items.text: Ukrainian borscht cooking was added to UNESCO's endangered heritage list in 2022.

items.title: Mriya
items.text: The world's largest aircraft, destroyed near Kyiv in 2022.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport, and Andriy Shevchenko won the Ballon d'Or in 2004. Ukraine co-hosted Euro 2012 with Poland. The pole vaulter Serhiy Bubka set 35 world records, and the high jumper Yaroslava Mahuchikh won Olympic gold in 2024.

items.title: Euro 2012
items.text: Co-hosted with Poland; the final was in Kyiv.

items.title: Serhiy Bubka
items.text: The first person to pole vault over 6 metres.

items.title: Klitschko brothers
items.text: Vitali and Wladimir both held world heavyweight boxing titles.
